prompt_text: I am planning a trip. Should I book on Airbnb, Vrbo, or Booking.com, and how do I find a good host?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer
- Use Airbnb if you want unique stays, lots of private-room options, strong guest protections and community-driven listings.  
- Use Vrbo if you need whole-home rentals for families/groups and prefer fewer shared-space listings.  
- Use Booking.com if you want the widest inventory (hotels + apartments), lots of last‑minute options, often instant booking and sometimes simpler cancellation/no service‑fee listings.  

Best choice depends on your trip type, priorities (price vs host interaction vs cancellation flexibility) — and it’s smart to compare the same property across platforms before booking.

How to choose a platform (by trip type)
- Family or group wanting an entire house: Vrbo (focus on whole-home) or Airbnb whole-home listings.  
- Solo traveler or looking for unique/creative stays, local hosts and experiences: Airbnb.  
- Business travel, hotels/serviced apartments, or last-minute/instant-book needs: Booking.com.  
- Fee-sensitive travelers: compare total price (platform fees, cleaning, deposits, taxes) across sites — the lowest nightly rate can be much higher once fees are added.

Practical checklist to find a good host/property
1. Filter and shortlist
   - Set dates, guest count, necessary amenities (Wi‑Fi, self check‑in, washer, workspace).  
   - Use filters for “entire place” if you want privacy. On Airbnb use “Superhost” filter; on Booking.com look at “Top Reviewed”/“Preferred partner” and on Vrbo use “Premier Host” or high-review filters where available.  
2. Read recent reviews (last 6–12 months)
   - Prioritize recent reviews mentioning cleanliness, accuracy of listing, communication, and check‑in. Look for repeat praise about the host’s responsiveness.  
3. Check the host profile and listing details
   - Look for a completed host profile, verified ID badge, clear photos, house rules, a detailed description, and a clear check‑in process (self check‑in or meet).  
4. Examine fees, cancellation policy and house rules
   - Check total price (nightly + cleaning + service + taxes) and security deposit. Make sure the cancellation policy matches your risk tolerance.  
5. Message the host before booking
   - Ask specific questions about things that matter to you (exact sleeping arrangements, noise, parking, Wi‑Fi speed, work desk, elevator if on a high floor, pets allowed, etc.) and note how quickly and clearly they respond.  
6. Look for red flags
   - Few or no reviews, poor or vague photos, unusually low price, host asks to pay off-platform or via wire transfer, long unanswered questions, recent abrupt negative reviews about cleanliness or fraud.  
7. After booking
   - Keep all communications on the platform, document the property condition with photos on arrival, and report issues through the platform for fastest resolution.

Message template to pre‑book a host (copy/modify)
Hi — I’m [name]. I’m traveling with [number] guests from [dates]. Quick questions before booking: Is the bedroom layout as shown (beds, mattress sizes)? How reliable is the Wi‑Fi (work video calls)? Is self check‑in available and where can we park? Are there any restrictions we should know about? Thanks — I look forward to your reply.
(Short, specific questions help test responsiveness.)

Safety and payment tips
- Always pay and communicate through the platform. Never wire money or accept outside payment requests.  
- Check the platform’s guest protection and cancellation/insurance options before booking.  
- If staying longer than a month, ask for references and consider a lease or written agreement for clarity.  
- On arrival, take timestamped photos of any existing damage and report issues promptly.

Red flags to cancel or avoid
- Host refuses to use platform payment or requests cash/wire transfer.  
- Multiple recent reviews citing the same problem (dirty, inaccurate listing, host no‑show).  
- Inconsistent or evasive replies to simple questions.

Quick decision guide
- Want unique stays and community features + solid guest support → Airbnb.  
- Need full houses for groups/families, fewer shared rooms → Vrbo.  
- Want broad choices including hotels, flexible last‑minute options, or sometimes lower/no service fees → Booking.com.  
- Always compare the same listing across platforms (price and total fees can differ).

If you tell me your destination, travel dates, how many people, and your top priorities (price, cancellation flexibility, private whole place, host interaction, work needs), I can recommend which platform is likely best and give a short list of what to search for.
